participants.note: reviewed chrono type handling and mock time access, and questioned the PR's relevance after #35496 merged
supported the setter approach over an options approach and requested test coverage
raised ergonomics concerns with per-object clock setting and suggested a callback clock abstraction
suggested using FakeNodeClock RAII helper in chainstatemanager tests

claims.harm: direct GetMockTime call in tx_pool test can silently cause bugs if mocktime is unset, bypasses the system time sanitizer, and returns a duration instead of a time point
claims.quote: the call to GetMockTime here looks wrong for several reasons: It directly access the test-only global of the mock time, which may be 0, and thus may lead to silent bugs if mocktime was not used here? It side-steps the g_used_system_time runtime sanitizer.

claims.harm: requiring users to manage clock time across multiple separate places is cumbersome and error-prone
claims.quote: This could get a bit annoying and potentially dangerous when users need to start managing clocks across multiple places.
claims.settled_by_quote: My instinct is that it doesn't because if you're creating multiple chainstate managers or other objects that accept times, and your application needs artificial times instead of the current clock time, I wouldn't assume that multiple objects would want to have the same time set.

claims.harm: the PR may no longer be relevant following the merge of PR 35496, and it conflicts conceptually with PR 35906
claims.quote: That one was merged, so is this here still relevant? Also, this conflicts with https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35906#discussion_r3726539086

support.reason: prefers setting clock time on chainman over setting it in options because it can be updated repeatedly and matches current global mocktime mechanics

result.notes: Initial record setup. Maflcko's query regarding relevance and conceptual conflict with PR 35906 remains open without an author reply.
